newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel chrmn sees div possible in 2004.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel chrmn sees div possible in 2004.

text.p: Eurotunnel co-chairman Patrick Ponsolle said on Monday the company could pay a dividend as early as 2004 if the company performed "very well".
"The first dividend could be paid in around 10 years or in 2004 if the company performs very well," Ponsolle told a news conference.
Eurotunnel unveiled a restructuring of its junior debt on Monday aimed at stabilising its financial situation.
It said in Paris that 8.0 billion francs ($1.5 billion) of its junior debt would be converted into shares at 10.40 francs per share.
The company also said it would issue eight billion francs of December 2003 convertible bonds that would be converted at a price of 12.40 francs per share.

The announcement was part of a debt restructuring deal aimed at insuring the long term viability of Eurotunnel. Under the agreement, shareholders will hold 54.5 percent of the company's capital after the restructuring. ($ = 5.174 French Francs)
